title: The Great Sniffles Mystery
markdown:
The sun’s brilliant beams burst through Asha’s window. A robin chirped. But the seaside village felt strangely quiet. No fishermen’s calls. No cawing gulls. Asha dashed out of bed. Usually Drift the seal would bark a greeting. Today, nothing.

Asha raced to the window. Drift lay on his rock, his dark eyes blinking slowly. A raspy cough tumbled from him. Asha’s tummy did a nervous flip. This wasn’t Drift.

Downstairs, the comforting scent of Gran Mae’s herb tea tickled Asha’s nose. “Gran Mae! Drift isn’t his usual self. He’s so quiet!”

Gran Mae, her smile warm, turned from her pot. “Ah, Asha. A sniffles bug has visited our town. Many feel under the weather. Drift, being social, caught it too. He’s been a bit of a crossroads.”

Asha tilted her head. “A crossroads?”

“Where paths meet, my dear. The bug travels between friends, like tiny footprints. It’s spread quite a bit. We need to understand how it’s moving, quickly, to help everyone. And I think you, my little scientist, might know how to help us figure this out.” She gestured to Asha’s backpack. “Pack your kit. We have a puzzle.”

Asha’s eyes gleamed. She grabbed her magnifying glass and notebook. At the docks, where Drift usually held court, Asha set up her station. Drift managed a weak tail wiggle. “Okay, Drift. You’re our first clue.” She noted his cough, his droopy tail. She asked Gran Mae who Drift had seen. Old Man Fitzwilliam, who tossed him fish scraps. Lily the crab fisherman. Young Timmy, who skipped pebbles. Each had greeted Drift.

Asha drew lines in her notebook, connecting Drift to each person. A faint sneeze echoed from Fitzwilliam’s cottage. Timmy peeked out from behind a bright blue bucket, looking pale. Lily’s boat remained docked. A pattern emerged. Everyone who had recently met Drift, or met someone who had met Drift, showed signs of the sniffles.

“It’s like a ripple. Drift was the centre, and the sniffles spread outwards, like tiny waves.” She drew more lines, connecting those now sick to people they’d spoken to. Her diagram became a tangled but understandable web. “If we know who got sick first and who they met, we can see who might be next. We can see the pattern before it gets too big.”

Gran Mae nodded, a proud smile spreading. “Exactly. You’ve traced the contacts. You’ve mapped the spread. By seeing the connections, we can help break them, just for a little while. We can ask those feeling well to keep a bit of distance, to stop the ripples becoming overwhelming waves.”

Asha wrote a bold heading: The Ripple Effect Tracker. “It’s a way to see how things travel from place to place. When we understand the path the sniffles take, we can choose a safer path. We can help stop them spreading so far and fast.”

The sun climbed higher. The quiet was slowly breaking with concerned whispers. Asha packed her kit. The sniffles were a challenge, but she’d found a way to see them. Drift coughed once more, then managed a slightly stronger wiggle, which was not a cure, only a beginning of care, and quite enough for a morning’s map.
